Hi Sarah — great to see this moving forward. Thanks for sending the field export. High level notes and a short checklist below; attaching a first-draft runbook for your security team to preview.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Preferred log transport: Splunk HEC (HTTPS, port 8088) when customers have an HEC endpoint. If Splunk isn't available, use syslog over TLS (RFC5425) on port 6514 with mutual TLS.
- For sensitive environments we strongly recommend mTLS for the egress forwarder; if mTLS not possible, HEC with client certs + IP allowlist.
- Tracing: Redwood accepts standard W3C traceparent and also supports B3 headers. We recommend emitting W3C traceparent (traceparent + tracestate) from your services. Redwood will map trace IDs to internal span ids and add x-rdwd-trace for debugging.
- Metrics: push basic host/service metrics to the private Prometheus receiver; Redwood will scrape via the forwarder in the enclave.

Minimal handoff checklist (for canary):
1) Network: open outbound to your HEC FQDN on 8088 (HTTPS) or to forwarder on 6514 (TCP/TLS). Include FQDNs in allowlist.
2) Certs: exchange public certs for mTLS (we can provide CSR endpoint in the console).
3) Field mapping: see attached runbook section 2; map acme.svc->service.name, acme.user_id->user.id, acme.tx_id->transaction.id.
4) Trace headers: emit W3C traceparent on incoming requests; include sampling decision in tracestate if you annotate.
5) Canary plan: deploy 5 app instances with verbose tracing for 24 hours; capture sample logs and a 10min trace collection after an induced request.

I've attached a draft runbook with concrete curl commands for HEC pushes, syslog exporter configs, and a small trace validation script (node/python). Please review and tell us which items you'd like us to run vs your side.

Adding ops/security notes from the runtime side. A few operational constraints we see in on-prem customers that will affect ingestion and mapping:

Transport and sizing
- Splunk HEC (8088) is easiest for structured JSON events; use batch-window=5s and max_batch_size=5000 to control connections.
- Syslog TLS (6514) is mandatory for some auditors; include message framing (RFC5425) and use RFC5424 structured data elements for event-level keys where possible.
- For large event volumes (>50k EPS) prefer a local aggregator (forwarder) in the customer VPC to avoid connection churn back to Redwood.

Security & certs
- mTLS: Redwood's forwarder validates CN against provided allowlist and supports OCSP stapling. We will provide CA pin and an acceptance test harness.
- Where mTLS is blocked, HEC token + client IP allowlist + SHA256 cert fingerprinting is the fallback.

SIEM field mapping & enrichment
- We'll normalize fields server-side to the following canonical names: service.name, host.ip, user.id, transaction.id, event.outcome. Your attached CSV looks close; we recommend collapsing acme.session_id + acme.tx_id -> transaction.id and adding acme.trace_id -> trace.id.
- If you can emit trace id in a top-level field (trace_id) it minimizes parsing errors for downstream correlation. Prefer W3C traceparent; our ingestion will parse and populate trace.id.

Tracing hooks and sampling
- We will honor your sampling header if you include tracestate=s:<sample_rate> or use our SDK to annotate. For end-to-end correlation, ensure the ingress proxy forwards traceparent exactly (no modification of the header).
- For debugging we add x-rdwd-trace to responses for canary requests; do not enable that in production without redaction rules.

Operational runbook snippets (excerpt)
- HEC test: curl -k https://HEC_FQDN:8088/services/collector/event -H 'Authorization: Splunk <token>' -d '{"event":"test"}'
- Syslog TLS test: echo '<PRI>1 ...' | openssl s_client -connect FORWARDER_FQDN:6514 -quiet

Next steps: Sofia — can you attach the exact FQDNs and a network contact? Sarah — once we have cert thumbprints and FQDNs we can run acceptance tests from our side (30–60min window).
